title: The future of the grid | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Energy Gang episode from the ACORE Grid Forum arguing the US cannot meet AI- and electrification-driven power demand by building new transmission alone, highlighting dynamic line ratings (Gridraven), battery-backed flexible data centres (Verrus), solid-state transformers (Expand Power Technologies) and bipartisan permitting reform.

insights.claim: Some US transmission projects have taken more than 20 years to complete and many others have been blocked entirely, while power demand rises rapidly from AI data centres, electrification and industrial growth.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Grid capacity constraints create a long runway for technologies that squeeze more out of existing assets.
insights.quote: Some transmission projects in the US have taken more than 20 years to complete. Many others have been blocked completely.

insights.claim: America cannot rely on building new infrastructure alone to meet its electricity needs; better use of existing grid capacity, demand flexibility and faster technology adoption will all be essential.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Investment opportunity shifts toward grid-enhancing tech and flexibility, not only wires and generation.
insights.quote: America cannot rely on building new infrastructure alone to meet its electricity needs.
insights.locator: Across the conversations, a common message

insights.claim: Gridraven CEO Georg Rute argues dynamic line ratings using advanced weather forecasting can increase the power existing transmission lines carry, and that the technology, despite seemingly slow adoption, is just beginning to take off.
insights.speaker: Georg Rute
insights.so_what: Dynamic line rating vendors may be at an adoption inflection point.
insights.quote: argues that the technology is just beginning to take off
insights.locator: Ed is joined first by Georg Rute

insights.claim: Verrus head of energy Jeff Bladen argues integrating large-scale battery storage into data centres lets them cut grid demand during peak stress without interrupting computing, potentially enabling faster grid connection.
insights.speaker: Jeff Bladen
insights.so_what: Flexible, battery-backed data centres could jump interconnection queues, a competitive edge for developers.
insights.quote: integrating large-scale battery storage into data centres can allow them to reduce their demand on the grid during periods of peak stress, without interrupting computing operations
insights.locator: Next Jeff Bladen, head of energy

insights.claim: The episode frames islanded, off-grid data-centre power systems as a missed opportunity compared with grid-connected flexible designs.
insights.speaker: Jeff Bladen
insights.so_what: Contrasts with the behind-the-meter/off-grid trend; grid-integrated flexibility may be the better value play.
insights.quote: why “islanded” off-grid power systems represent a missed opportunity
insights.locator: Next Jeff Bladen, head of energy

insights.claim: Traditional transformers have changed little in more than a century, and growing demand has pushed equipment lead times to several years.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Transformer shortages are a binding constraint on grid expansion, supporting pricing for incumbents and openings for new tech.
insights.quote: Traditional transformers have changed little in more than a century, and growing demand has pushed equipment lead times to several years.
insights.locator: Then Ed speaks to Carla Pinzón

insights.claim: Expand Power Technologies CEO Carla Pinzón argues semiconductor-based solid-state transformers could be a smaller, more flexible alternative able to manage both AC and DC and support solar, batteries and data centres.
insights.speaker: Carla Pinzón
insights.so_what: Power semiconductors could enter grid equipment, a potential new demand vector for the chip supply chain.
insights.locator: Then Ed speaks to Carla Pinzón

insights.claim: ACORE CEO Ray Long discusses prospects for bipartisan permitting reform, which could significantly cut the time needed to approve new transmission and generation projects.
insights.speaker: Ray Long
insights.so_what: Permitting reform passage would be a catalyst for transmission and generation developers.
insights.quote: bipartisan permitting reform, which could significantly reduce the time needed to approve new transmission and generation projects
insights.locator: Finally, Ed is joined by Ray Long

insights.claim: Political uncertainty has affected investment in US renewable energy, and long-term policy stability matters to developers and investors, while the clean energy industry must rebuild public confidence in its affordability and reliability.
insights.speaker: Ray Long
insights.so_what: Policy volatility is raising the risk premium on US renewables capital.
insights.locator: Finally, Ed is joined by Ray Long
